caption.text:
Grief doesn’t just take something from you — it reshapes you. It teaches you what it means to hold love with nowhere to place it, to carry memories that no longer have a home in the present. 

It’s not just missing them. It’s the quiet moments that follow — the instinct to reach for them, the way their absence shows up in the smallest parts of your day. It’s learning how to exist in a world that kept moving when something inside of you paused. 

And maybe the hardest part isn’t only that they’re gone, but that it changes how you trust, how you open up, how you let people in again. You wonder if your heart will ever feel safe the same way it once did. 

But grief is also proof that you loved deeply. That something real existed. And even if you carry it with you forever, it doesn’t mean you won’t find your way back to warmth, to connection, to feeling whole again — in a different way, but still whole. 🖤

Read more in the book ‘Altar’ by Tori Gordon 📖
